query: A positive interval reaches the old continuation margin after the comparator pool expands. Would you continue allocation at 128 and why?
answer: Stop under the mean-margin rule. The corrected estimated mean, 0.035299, is below 0.04 even though the ordinary interval is positive and includes the margin.
scope: Post hoc same-world correction on 24 authored worlds, without fresh confirmation or evidence of zero benefit.

query: Suppose an effect has already committed, but neither projected status view can be contacted. Is a safe hold still the expected route?
answer: All three paths hold in that cell despite the exact prior effect.
scope: One authored case with both projections unavailable. The result supplies no rate for real outages or production holds.

query: The verifier cache service replied without an error but was behind a release revocation. Which decision do the two comparators make?
answer: Both arms call the specialist when the successful index response is stale under the current revocation.
scope: The matched authored decision supplies the currently required revision. It does not establish how independent revocation delivery behaves.

query: An earlier verifier certificate has aged out by the serving deadline across separate local processes. What happens to its fallback?
answer: Both arms defer to the specialist after the fallback expiry at logical tick 3.
scope: Same-owner process separation and one authored decision. It does not address a production race between authorization and use.

query: Has a whole board program ever stopped verifying solely because its queue prioritizes expanded length, with the number of proposals fixed?
answer: Yes in the b24 cell. Handle depth verifies and expanded length exhausts under the fixed 96-proposal budget.
scope: A descriptive query and one authored routing case. Exhaustion under one priority does not show infeasibility or establish a general ranking.

query: Both shipment dashboards show the same supplier delivery alert before cutoff. What new observation would justify recording physical receipt?
answer: A separate dock observation of this shipment before cutoff could corroborate delivery. The replicated alert supports one reported event.
scope: Authored provenance exercise. The observations must refer to the same shipment and cutoff, and the result supplies no field reliability estimate.

query: Deep slots are fewer when chunk boundaries are learned. Can our serving team budget a fixed throughput gain on heterogeneous batches?
answer: Abstain on the throughput gain. Deep shortening is compatible with variable chunk counts and different batching and memory costs.
scope: The paper's evaluation compares model/data/compute conditions. It does not measure an end-to-end service with the proposed length distribution.

query: The proof checks that an audit consumer rejects a receipt making a deployed-transport overclaim. Can that prove a different compiled program safe?
answer: No. The local formal target concerns the finite gate and its overclaim or mutation-control rejection rules.
scope: Separate the finite modeled consumer acceptance contract and its authored controls from the external named compile receipt and from any general deployment safety claim.

query: What is the expected person-time saving per incident at a production receiver when we move the second status call into the gateway?
answer: Abstain on person-time. The evidence records equal matched closure and a tradeoff between caller requests and status bytes.
scope: Four authored tasks in local same-owner conditions. No operator-time or production rate measurement.

query: The sensor drops out in the violent part of a maneuver. Does a good average frame-level prediction-set rate certify the complete episode?
answer: No. Calibrate and evaluate for the maneuver-level decision using the relevant grouping and missingness regime.
scope: Coverage has a defined unit, conditions and population. Informative missingness and dependence block automatic transfer from frames to episodes.
